articles.summary: Key Takeaways NetSuite’s Automated Cash Application imports bank lines and matches invoices only when data is clean. Exceptions return to your finance team. Oracle’s own docs confirm NetSuite can import a bank line without matching any customer payment, leaving you to pick the customer and create the payment by hand. NetSuite treats the bank line as its unit of work, so exact amount-and-reference matching stalls when payment data goes incomplete. A lump-sum ACH covering six invoices with a short-pay on two defeats the rule-based matching engine outright. Most B2B payment detail arrives scattered across email, PDFs, or portal exports, data NetSuite’s exact-match logic cannot reconcile alone. NetSuite has no native intelligent exception-handling workflow, so teams often write custom scripts to route failed matches into a queue. Batch bank feeds and separate GL uploads create the daily delays and reconciliation blind spots. Where NetSuite quits before the finish line NetSuite’s Automated Cash Application stops short. It imports bank lines and matches them to open invoices when data is clean, but the moment a payment lacks a clear reference, automation hands the work back to you.
